title: Reconstruction of the binding pathway of an anti-HIV drug, Indinavir, in complex with the HTLV-1 protease by Unaggregated Unbiased Molecular Dynamics simulation
one_liner_zh: 该文用无偏分子动力学模拟重建HIV药物Indinavir与HTLV-1蛋白酶的结合路径，虽涉及蛋白-配体互作和MD方法，但对象为蛋白酶-小分子而非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题TF-DNA结合机制无直接关联。
abstract: Retroviruses are a growing concern for the health of human beings, and one of the dangerous members of this family is the Human T-cell Leukemia Virus 1 (HTLV-1) virus. It has affected more than 20 million people so far, and since there are no registered treatments against it yet, urgent treatment solutions are needed. One of the most promising drug targets to fight this virus is the protease enzyme of the virus’s protein machinery. In this study, by utilizing a computational method called Unaggregated Unbiased Molecular Dynamics (UUMD), we reconstructed the binding pathway of a HTLV-1 protease inhibitor, Indinavir, to find the details of the binding pathway, the influential residues, and also the stable states of the binding pathway. We achieved the native conformation of the inhibitor in 6 rounds, 360 replicas by performing over 4 micro-seconds of UMD simulations. We found 3 Intermediate states between the solvated state and the native conformation state in the binding pathway. We also discovered that aromatic residues such as Trp98 and Trp98′, catalytic residues Asp32 and Asp32′, and the flap region’s residues have the most influential roles in the binding pathway and also have the most contribution to the total interaction energies. We believe that the details found in this study would be a great guide for developing new treatment solutions against the HTLV-1 virus by inhibiting the HTLV-1 protease.
abstract_zh: 逆转录病毒对人类健康的威胁日益增加，该家族中的危险成员之一是人类T细胞白血病病毒1型（HTLV-1）。迄今已有超过2000万人受其影响，且目前尚无注册的治疗方法，因此亟需有效的治疗方案。对抗该病毒最有前景的药物靶点之一是其蛋白质机制中的蛋白酶酶。在本研究中，通过利用一种名为无聚集无偏分子动力学（UUMD）的计算方法，我们重建了HTLV-1蛋白酶抑制剂Indinavir的结合通路，以揭示结合通路的细节、关键残基以及结合通路的稳定状态。我们通过进行超过4微秒的UMD模拟，在6轮、360个副本中获得了抑制剂的天然构象。在结合通路中，我们发现了溶剂化状态与天然构象状态之间的3个中间态。我们还发现，芳香族残基如Trp98和Trp98′、催化残基Asp32和Asp32′，以及瓣膜区域的残基在结合通路中发挥最关键作用，并对总相互作用能的贡献最大。我们相信，本研究中发现的细节将为通过抑制HTLV-1蛋白酶来开发针对HTLV-1病毒的新治疗方案提供重要指导。
